ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of sneezing in Shia hadith, and what is the consequence for those who deny the Prophet's share in it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights sneezing as both a physical benefit and a spiritual reminder of Allah, countering skeptics who deny the Prophet's specific connection to this act by asserting that their denial would forfeit their share in his intercession. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's comprehensive role in daily acts of worship, linking bodily functions to divine remembrance. The reference to intercession (Shafa'ah) serves as a theological guarantee of the truth of the Prophet's teachings against those who dismiss them.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The sneezing is a good thing. It is beneficial for the body, and reminds you of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’. I said, ‘In our presence there is a group of people who are saying, ‘There is no share for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in the sneezing’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they were lying, so may they not attain the intercession of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’’.
en.sarwar: 8. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al- Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Sneezing is a good thing. It benefits the body and reminds one of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’ I then said, ‘Nearby to us there are people who say, “There is nothing in sneezing for the Messenger of Allah.” The Imam said, ‘If they are lying, the intercession of Muhammad will not avail them.’”
